title: Seed stitch wrist warmers
subtitle: Flat wrist warmers in moss stitch with no thumb hole.
excerpt: Short wrist warmers in DK wool, knitted flat in moss stitch (UK) and seamed up the side. No thumb hole, no shaping. Cast on, work straight, seam, wear. Sized for wrist circumferences of 16, 18, and 20 cm.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 2nd series (1880s), §Wrist-band. Simple knitted wrist-bands in textured stitches are among the oldest patterns in the Weldon's archive; moss-stitch and seed-stitch variants appear across multiple volumes.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4 mm needles. Moss stitch at the same needle size is slightly denser; the wrist-warmer width is set by the cast-on count rather than gauge.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wrist circumference 16 (18, 20) cm. Length from cast-on to cast-off 12 cm on all sizes.

glossaryTerms.definition: A textured stitch worked by alternating knit and purl on every stitch, swapping the order each row so the knits and purls never stack. This is called seed stitch in US terminology. UK moss stitch and US seed stitch produce the same fabric.

content.text: Wrist warmers in DK wool, knitted flat and seamed, sized for wrist circumferences of 16, 18, and 20 cm.
These are worked flat in a single piece, seamed up the side with a short gap left for the thumb. The stitch throughout is
moss stitch (UK)

, which is the same fabric as US seed stitch. The flat construction makes these a good first seamed project and suits knitters who prefer straight needles. Budget about 60 g (130 m / 140 yards) of DK yarn for both wrist warmers. They fit under coat sleeves for cold weather and double as fingerless mitts for indoor desk work.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 60 g (about 130 m / 140 yards) of DK-weight yarn
items.substitutions: Any DK-weight wool or wool blend. Cotton is workable but has less elasticity in the seam.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) straight or circular needles

items.name: Tapestry needle
items.qty: 1, blunt-tipped, for seaming and weaving in ends

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches per 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4 mm needles. For these wrist warmers the cast-on count controls the width directly, so the gauge is a starting point rather than a strict requirement. If your gauge differs, check the finished width of a tension swatch before casting on: 18 stitches at your gauge should measure 16 (18, 20) cm when laid flat.
Stitches used

Moss stitch (UK): *k1, p1* across on every RS row and WS row, swapping so that knits sit above purls and purls sit above knits. The trick is to never knit a knit or purl a purl: look at the stitch on the needle and work the opposite of what you see.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for wrist circumferences 16 (18, 20) cm.
Cast on

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 34 (38, 42) stitches. These stitch counts include two edge stitches that become the seam allowance; they are not part of the stitch pattern. For the long-tail method at 42 stitches, pull off about 27 cm of tail before starting.
Wrist warmer body
Row 1 (RS): k1 (edge), *k1, p1* to last stitch, k1 (edge).
Row 2 (WS): k1 (edge), *p1, k1* to last stitch, k1 (edge).
Repeat rows 1 and 2 until the piece measures 12 cm from the cast-on edge. Bind off in pattern: *k1, p1, pass first stitch over*; repeat to end.
Stitch count check-in: you should have 34 (38, 42) stitches throughout. Moss stitch does not decrease; if your count changes, a stitch was dropped or accidentally added.
Seaming

Fold the piece in half with right sides together, lining up the cast-on and bind-off edges. Seam from the cast-on edge upwards for 4 (4, 4.5) cm using mattress stitch, then leave a 3.5 (4, 4) cm gap for the thumb, then seam the remaining length to the top. The gap sits where the base of the thumb meets the wrist.
Mirror your second wrist warmer

Work the second wrist warmer as a mirror of the first by reversing the thumb gap direction when seaming: seam from the top down for 4 (4, 4.5) cm, leave the thumb gap, then seam the remaining length. Hold the first wrist warmer thumb-gap-up: the gap sits on the right. The second wrist warmer's gap should sit on the left when worn.
Common faults

Moss stitch reverts to rib: the most common error. This happens when you knit a knit and purl a purl instead of swapping. Check each stitch before working it: the stitch on the needle should look like a V (a knit stitch from below) and you should purl it, or like a bump (a purl stitch) and you should knit it.
Seam twists the wrist warmer: the two cast-on edges were not aligned before seaming. Pin the bottom edges together first, then seam upwards.
Thumb gap in the wrong place on the second wrist warmer: both gaps end up on the same side. Reverse the seam start point on the second one as described above.
Finishing
Weave all yarn tails in on the wrong side, running them along the seam line for at least 5 cm. Press the seam gently with a damp cloth if needed to flatten any ridge.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Lay flat to dry. The flat construction means these dry faster than a knitted-in-the-round mitt.
What to try next

The in-the-round version of the same wrist warmer requires no seaming and teaches the magic-loop or DPN technique. A cable column added to the back of the hand is the natural decoration to introduce after the plain version.
